extracted.intended_audience: patent chemical indexers / patent examiners / database coders (chemical/sterol indexing)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and code-assigning standards for chemical indexing of patent documents, with detailed coding schemes for pharmaceutical formulations, devices, analytical methods, packaging, and an extensive steroid-descriptor code system (Parts S, T, U).

rubrics_metrics.name: R1: General terms for Galenicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes R111, R112, R120, R130, R140, R150, R160, R170 denote general galenical/formulation features (Novel dosage form; Novel production of dosage form; Coated form; Disposable; Ink; label; Multicomponent; Reference standard; Special shape).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The codes R111 and R112 are used in combination with an R0: code for the particular dosage form.

rubrics_metrics.name: R2: Routes of pharmaceutical administration
rubrics_metrics.description: R200-R290 map to specific administration routes (e.g., buccal; sublingual; external/topical; implant; injection; infusion; intraarterial; intravenous; intraaural; intranasal/intratracheal; intraocular; intramuscular; subcutaneous; transdermal; intrauterine; intravaginal; oral; rectal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searchability note: Transdermal is marked 'Searchable since 1983/Week 37'. Use the exact route code when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additives coding and cross-referencing (R3/R-Additives note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additives (e.g., absorbent, accelerator, adhesive, buffer, chelating agent, coating, diluent, dye, flavour, gelling agent, lubricant, plasticiser, propellant, stabiliser types, surfactant, suspending agent) are listed (R301-R320) but additives themselves are indexed in M0-M5 while their uses are coded in Part Q when the additive itself is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a particular stabiliser used in a formulation -> additive indexed in M2 with appropriate Q: codes; the formulation is covered in M6 with appropriate R: codes. Follow this split coding to avoid mis-indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: R4: Pharmaceutical administration devices
rubrics_metrics.description: R410-R463 cover devices such as catheter, dosage into orifice, implanting device, inhalation device, injection gun and syringes (R46 subcodes: general, hypodermic, remote control, syringe needle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign device-specific R: codes; when a syringe is present use R46 family codes and appropriate subcode for needle or remote control features.

rubrics_metrics.name: R5: Processes; Apparatuses; Machines — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: R50: General classification; R501 (Physical process or apparatus) and R502 (Chemical process or apparatus) are only used for processes/apparatuses that cannot be more specifically coded elsewhere in Set R5:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the most specific R5: subset code available; use R501/R502 only as catch-alls.

rubrics_metrics.name: R51: Analytical; diagnostic; testing categories
rubrics_metrics.description: R510: General analytical/diagnostic/testing; R511 automated analysis/diagnosis/test; R512 chromatographic; R513 isotope detection; R514 spectroscopic/colorimetric; R515 other processes/apparatuses for analysis/diagnosis/testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes introduced/annotated with (1981) where applicable. Use the technique-specific code (e.g., chromatographic) where the document specifies the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: R52/R53: Other processes and apparatuses (R5 subsets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers agglutination/precipitation, biological/fermentation, coating, compression/vacuum, cooling/freezing, cutting/grinding, distilling/heating, drying/lypholisation, electrical/magnetic, filling, flow control/transporting (excluding aerosol cans/valves, coded R700), forming/moulding, impregnating, microscopy/optical, mixing, purification/separation (excl. drying/lypholisation), radiation, sampling, spraying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If process is listed, select the corresponding R52/R53 code; cross-reference related codes (e.g., forming also see R523). Exclusions noted (e.g., aerosol cans -> R700).

rubrics_metrics.name: R6: Diagnostic and analytical methods — materials, reagents, substances detected
rubrics_metrics.description: R61: Material tested (blood/plasma; urine; other body fluid; other material). R62: Reagent used (antibody; antigen; colour indicator; enzyme; fluorescent-labelled; isotopically/radioactively labelled; other reagent). R63: Substance detected (antibody; antigen; enzyme; drug; fat; microorganism; pesticide/agrochemical; protein; steroid; other substance detected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coding notes: many R6 codes annotated (1981). A substance is coded R633 only if no other code in Subset R63: is applicable. Use the most specific material/reagent/substance code available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R7: Packaging codes and legacy note
rubrics_metrics.description: R700-R770 map to packaging forms (Aerosol can and valve; Ampoule; Bottle; Box/carton; Bag/blister/bubble pack; Cap/closure; Dispenser; Safety container).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Prior to 1976 N101 was assigned to pharmaceutical packaging materials (Farmdoc – Part B:). Use R7 codes for post-1976 documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steroid selection criteria (what is a 'steroid' for coding)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be indexed as a steroid, a structure must contain a complete cyclopenta(a)phenanthrene ring system; the ring system may have additional fused rings but cannot be broken (no secosteroids), cannot have carbon atoms in the ring replaced by heteroatoms (no oxa-steroids), and rings cannot vary in size from the basic system (no nor- or homo-steroids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steroid codes are defined with ring letters A–D and positions 1–23. Steroids are coded when they appear as starting material, intermediate, end product, or component in a composition. Historical note: prior to 1981, all steroid codes on a patent were overcoded in one field causing false combinations; from 1981 onward, codes for individual steroids are listed in separate subfields (starting materials, intermediates, end-products, components) to avoid false combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of steroid codes (2A / 2B / position and exo rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Set in Parts S:, T:, and U: covers a single steroid feature. 2A-terms indicate the position on the steroid nucleus (last two digits 01–23 correspond to positions). Codes ending in '00' indicate the feature is 'exo' (not directly bonded to nucleus). Codes ending '23' indicate position 23 or higher. 2B-terms are additional codes (last two digits 30 or higher) needed when 2A does not fully describe a feature (e.g., specify acyl group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indented 2A/2B definitions: an indented definition is only assigned if the closest preceding unindented definition is also assigned. Hyphens indicate positions where a particular feature cannot occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which Parts code which steroid/chemical features (Parts A–W applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mapping notes: Parts A–C (elements present); Parts D–G (ring systems) — the steroid nucleus itself is not assigned a RIN but spiro/fused complete systems get RIN; Functional groups bonded to steroid nucleus are coded in Parts S–U (not in H,J,K,L); Part M miscellaneous descriptors (from 1981 forward include specific codes such as M417 incomplete structure, M430/M431 composition active ingredients); Part N reactions/processes; Parts P/Q activities and uses (from 1981 forward all codes); Part R formulations; Part V natural products/polymers; Part W dye descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use S/T/U for steroid nucleus functional groups; employ other parts (M,N,P,Q,R,V,W) as indicated by feature and date (pre- vs post-1981 differences highlighted).

rubrics_metrics.name: S0: Carbon–carbon double bond coding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: 2A-terms list positions for C=C bonds (positions 1–23). In coding positional location of a double bond, the lower number of the pair is recorded (e.g., for 4,5 record 4; for 17(20) record 17). Exo double bonds include unsaturated methylene groups connected to the nucleus. Aromatic A ring is coded as positions 1,3,5 in 2-A and further specified in 2-B terms (e.g., 1(2), 5(10) and 'aromatic A' in 2-B). Double bonds common to two rings have specific treatments (listed examples: 5(10), 8(9), 13(14) referenced to ring identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lower-number convention for 2-A field; use 2-B terms for distinctions where 2-A is not definitive (positions 1,5,8,9,13,20).

rubrics_metrics.name: S1: Ring saturation and substitution coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes (e.g., S110, S113, S120) indicate H at positions 10, 13, 20 — used only when hydrogen at those positions indicates absence of a methyl group at 18, 19 or 21 respectively. Not used for a 17-methyl group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these codes only to indicate absence of methyl where specifically relevant at the listed positions; do not use for 17-methyl.

rubrics_metrics.name: S2: Alpha (allo) configuration coding rules and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: S2 codes indicate alpha (allo) configuration at positions (exo, 1–23). The alpha descriptor may be implied and coded where configuration is known from trivial names (e.g., cholic acid). When a steroidal carbon is substituted such that one of the groups must be alpha-oriented (no hydrogens present), the alpha descriptor is automatically coded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some codes (9-alpha, 14-alpha) are assumed and not coded unless substituent is other than H. i-compounds have specific 2-B punches. Caution: coder omissions are possible; alpha descriptors should not be solely relied upon for complete searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: S3: Beta configuration — explicit-only coding
rubrics_metrics.description: S3 codes indicate beta configuration at positions (exo, 1–23) but are only used when the document specifically states the beta configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beta is never implied and therefore may not be relied on for complete searches. The 5-B code is not used unless substituent is other than hydrogen. Because coding of alpha/beta can be arbitrary, do not use these descriptors if a complete search is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: S4: Miscellaneous chemical groups and Rules of Superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: S4 codes represent any group not provided by other 2-A terms (examples: O-Na, azides N3, Grignard intermediates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule of Superiority: the Miscellaneous code is used only if no other designation is applicable. In cases of doubt between C-sub and Misc., the C-sub code takes precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: S5: Hydroxy (–OH) positional coding
rubrics_metrics.description: S5 2A terms code hydroxy substituents at positions Exo and 1–23 (S500–S523).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding hydroxy groups, use the position-specific S5 codes; combine with appropriate 2-B terms if needed to describe O-containing substituents (see S7/S8 for related acyl/ether distinctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: S6: Keto positional coding and omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: S6 codes record keto substituents at specific positions (Exo and positions 1–23) with some positions not applicable (hyphens shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the provided position codes; note hyphens indicate positions where a keto cannot occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: S7: Acyloxy (O-acyl) coding — need for 2B terms to specify acyl
rubrics_metrics.description: S7 2A terms indicate position of acyloxy groups; additional 2B-terms (S730–S770 etc.) specify the 'Type of O-acyl group present' (carboxylic, poly, unsaturated, substituted, aromatic, aliphatic straight/branched/cycloaliphatic, heterocyclic, inorganic types including phosphorus, SO4, osmium, boron, N/S/O/Halo-containing, miscellaneous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The -O-Acyl designation refers to an ester attached through the -O- atom. Multiple coding principle applies: all applicable 2-B terms should be applied (e.g., code carboxylic, aromatic, substituted, O-containing and exo-OH when appropriate). Examples illustrating multi-term coding are provided in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: S8: O‑R (ether) coding and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: S8 2A terms code ether linkages (R-O-R) where one R is part of the steroid nucleus (positions Exo, 1–23). 2-B defines the type of R (hydrocarbon, N-containing, S-containing, O-containing, halo-containing, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: epoxides where two carbons linked by single oxygen are present are coded as epoxy unless the oxygen is part of a lactone (then 'epoxy' not used). Do not code acetals/ketals under O-R (they are handled elsewhere). Special rules for O-hetero coding when side-chain carbons 20–23+ are involved; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: S9: Epoxy coding
rubrics_metrics.description: S9 codes record epoxy groups attached to two nuclear carbon atoms; the two positions to which the epoxy is attached are recorded (positions Exo, 1–23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epoxy is used for a ring epoxide attached to two nucleus carbons; record both positions in 2-A.

rubrics_metrics.name: T0: Ketal (and related ketal/acetal) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: T0 codes designate ketal/acetals (reaction product of a keto or aldehyde with an alcohol), including thioketal, semithioketal, acetal, thioacetal and hemithioacetal. Non-cyclic ketals (acetals) should also be coded under the 2-B term 'Bis-substituents'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclic oxygen ketals are not coded in O-hetero 2-A/2-B. Cyclic thioketals are not coded under S-hetero in 2-A but are coded as thioketal in 2-B.

rubrics_metrics.name: T1: Heterocyclic ring with O (O‑hetero) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: T1 codes record oxygen-containing heterocyclic rings attached to the steroid nucleus (positions Exo, 1–23) and specify ring types (morpholine, furan, lactone, spirostane, pseudosapogenin, acetonide, peroxide, pyran, other). Type of attachment is recorded (spiro, fused, independent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions: acid/anhydride adducts, epoxides, cyclic oxygen ketals, and steroidal sapogenins are excluded from O-hetero. When hetero ring involves side-chain carbons 18–23+, record point of attachment. Use 2-A/2-B combinations to fully describe fused/spiro/independent cases; examples illustrate coding (e.g., fused lactone/furan coded as 11,13-O-hetero; furan; fused).

rubrics_metrics.name: T2: Halogen positional and type coding
rubrics_metrics.description: T2 codes record halogen substituents at positions Exo and 1–23 with 2-B codes for specific halogens present (T230 Fluorine, T231 Chlorine, T232 Bromine, T233 Iodine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record position-specific halogen codes and use the specific-halogen 2-B designation(s). Special steroid categories (e.g., pseudosapogenins) have additional coding notes elsewhere in T1.

rubrics_metrics.name: T3: -S-R, -Se-R, -Te-R substituent coding
rubrics_metrics.description: T3 2A codes mark substituents joined to the steroid nucleus by sulfur, selenium, or tellurium atoms (positions Exo, 1–23). 2-B distinguishes -Se-R, -Te-R, =S(Se,Te), R=H, and R not H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions: S-containing heterocyclics are excluded (these are in T4). When coding exo =S, exclude cases where =S is part of an acyl group. NCS/SCN handled elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: T4: S-heterocyclic ring coding
rubrics_metrics.description: T4 codes record sulfur-containing heterocycles attached to nucleus (positions Exo, 1–23) and specify specific rings (thiophene, thiazole, thioketal, other) and attachment type (spiro, fused, independent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the same ring-attachment coding conventions as O-hetero. 'Thioketal' is coded under ketal descriptors and not as S-hetero 2-A. Examples provided (e.g., thiirane coded under 'misc').

rubrics_metrics.name: T5: N‑R‑R (nitrogen substituents) coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: T5 codes indicate nitrogen-containing groups attached via nitrogen (positions Exo, 1–23). 2-B categories include primary/secondary/tertiary amine, quaternary ammonium, NO2/NO/miscellaneous, R is acyl (amide), imino.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N‑R‑R excludes nitrogen atoms that are part of heterocyclic rings (those are T6). When amine is acylated, code R=Acyl. Exclude (=N)-ketone reagents from N‑R‑R category.

rubrics_metrics.name: T6: N-heterocyclic ring coding
rubrics_metrics.description: T6 codes record nitrogen-containing heterocycles (positions Exo, 1–23) and list specific ring types (morpholine, piperidine, pyridine, pyrimidine, azole, pyrrolidine, thiazole, piperazine, other) and attachment type (spiro, fused, independent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding N-hetero rings follow the O-hetero attachment rules. Several 2-B descriptors further define specific ring types; some rings may also be coded as O-hetero where appropriate (e.g., morpholine).

rubrics_metrics.name: T7: Keto reagent (derivatization) coding
rubrics_metrics.description: T7 codes designate reaction products of a keto or aldehyde group with keto reagents (positions Exo, 1–23). 2-B specific groups include hydrazone, oxime, semicarbazone, Girard reagent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Girard reagents are coded as a separate category (not as hydrazones) and are not split into 'exo' terms except for halogens. When uncommon exo groups are present record them (e.g., cyano groups in dicyano phenylhydrazone). Substituents coded here are not to be recoded under N‑R‑R.

rubrics_metrics.name: T8: Methyl group coding conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: T8 codes indicate methyl groups at positions (1–23) but are not used at positions 10, 13, 20, 22 or 23+ because methyls at those positions are considered integral parts of the steroid nucleus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a methyl group is coded, also code the 2A term 'hydrocarbon chain' (U001-U023) and the 2B term 'lower alkyl (1–7)'. The 'exo' CH3 descriptor is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: T9: -C≡C- (ethynyl) coding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: T9 codes record ethynyl substituents (-C≡C-) at positions Exo, 1–23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this ethynyl code is used, also code 'hydrocarbon chain' (U001–U023) and 'alkynyl' (U035).

rubrics_metrics.name: U0: Hydrocarbon chain coding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: U0 codes represent hydrocarbon chains attached to the steroid nucleus (Exo, 1–23). 2-B defines chain types: lower alkyl (1–7 C), higher alkyl (>7 C), =CH2, alkenyl, with aromatic ring, alkynyl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not code methyls at 10/13 as hydrocarbon chain. In pregnanes the 2-carbon chain at position 17 is not coded unless substituted. In cholesterols/sterols certain chains are integral and not coded. 'Exo'-HC chain is not coded except in conjunction with 'exo' -C≡C- descriptor.

rubrics_metrics.name: U1: Carbocyclic ring coding (size, attachment, saturation)
rubrics_metrics.description: U1 codes record hydrocarbon rings attached to the nucleus (positions 1–23) with 2-B terms for ring size (3–7+ membered), attachment type (spiro, fused, independent) and ring type (saturated, unsaturated non-aromatic, aromatic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ring is fused, record the positions on the ring to which it is attached. The 'exo'-HC ring descriptor is not used. Apply 2-B ring-size and saturation descriptors as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: U2: -CN (cyano) positional coding
rubrics_metrics.description: U2 codes record cyano (-CN) substituents at positions Exo and 1–23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the position-specific U2 code corresponding to the location of the cyano group.

rubrics_metrics.name: U3: -COOR (ester) positional coding
rubrics_metrics.description: U3 codes record ester (-COOR) substituents at positions Exo and 1–23 and include 2-B terms to describe the type of ester group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply position-specific U3 codes and supplement with 2-B terms to indicate ester type per the guide's definitions (continued in next pages).
